title: Practice Exam 6
description: An additional full-length 36-question simulated California Class C knowledge exam. Challenging level.

questions.question: You are in the far-right freeway lane and want to reach the far-left lane two lanes over. You should:
choices: Change one lane at a time, signaling and checking the blind spot for each move
Cross both lanes in one smooth motion
Signal once and drift across both lanes
Cross quickly before traffic closes the gap
questions.explanation: Move over one lane at a time, completing each change—signal, mirror, blind-spot check—before starting the next. Crossing multiple lanes at once is unsafe and often illegal.

questions.question: A broken white line on your right separates your lane from an added lane at an on-ramp. It tells you:
choices: Traffic may merge there; be ready to adjust as vehicles enter
You must exit the freeway
No vehicles may cross it
The shoulder begins
questions.explanation: A broken white line marks where lanes meet and merging occurs. Watch for entering traffic and adjust speed or position to let them in safely.

questions.question: Heavy stop-and-go traffic fills the freeway. To merge from an on-ramp you should:
choices: Take turns ('zipper merge'), matching the slow speed and entering one car at a time
Stop on the ramp and wait for the freeway to clear
Force your way in at full speed
Drive on the shoulder past the slow traffic
questions.explanation: In congestion, vehicles should alternate (zipper merge). Match the slow traffic speed and ease in one at a time rather than stopping or forcing in.

questions.question: On the freeway you should generally position your car so that you:
choices: Stay out of other drivers' blind spots and avoid driving alongside them for long
Drive directly beside a truck for company
Match the exact position of the car ahead
Stay in the left lane regardless of speed
questions.explanation: Avoid lingering in blind spots or riding alongside other vehicles. Drift ahead or fall back so you're visible and have escape room.

questions.question: You park on a fairly level street but you're unsure if it's perfectly flat. The safest habit is to:
choices: Turn the wheels toward the curb and set the parking brake anyway
Leave the wheels straight and skip the parking brake on level ground
Leave it in neutral so it can be pushed if needed
Turn the wheels toward the road
questions.explanation: When unsure of the slope, turn the wheels toward the curb and always set the parking brake. It costs nothing and prevents a roll-away.

questions.question: A curb is painted red. You may:
choices: Not stop, stand, or park there at any time
Stop briefly to drop off a passenger
Park for under five minutes
Stand there while the engine runs
questions.explanation: A red curb means absolutely no stopping, standing, or parking—not even briefly. The other curb colors allow limited stops; red allows none.

questions.question: You want to back out of a perpendicular parking space in a busy lot. Before and while reversing you should:
choices: Check behind the car, then back slowly while watching for pedestrians and cross traffic
Rely only on the backup camera and reverse quickly
Back out fast before another car comes
Honk once and reverse without looking
questions.explanation: Walk-behind hazards and cross traffic are common in lots. Look behind before moving, back slowly, and keep scanning—cameras don't show everything.

questions.question: A work zone reduces a 65 mph freeway to 55 mph with cones. Driving 65 there is:
choices: Illegal and likely subject to a doubled fine
Legal because the original limit was 65
Legal if no workers are visible
Allowed in the left lane only
questions.explanation: The posted work-zone limit replaces the normal one. Exceeding it is illegal, and fines in active work zones are commonly doubled.

questions.question: Cresting a steep hill where you can't see oncoming traffic on a two-lane road, you should:
choices: Slow down, keep right, and never pass
Speed up to clear the crest quickly
Move toward the center for a better view
Pass now, since oncoming cars will see you
questions.explanation: A hillcrest hides oncoming traffic, so it's a no-passing situation. Slow down and keep well to the right until you can see the road ahead.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Hills and Curves

questions.question: Driving down a long, steep grade, the best way to control speed and save your brakes is to:
choices: Shift to a lower gear and use engine braking, braking only as needed
Ride the brakes the whole way down
Shift to neutral and coast
Turn off the engine to slow down
questions.explanation: On long downgrades, a lower gear lets the engine help hold your speed so the brakes don't overheat and fade. Coasting in neutral is unsafe and illegal.

questions.question: A pedestrian is crossing mid-block (not at an intersection) where there is no crosswalk. You should:
choices: Slow or stop as needed to avoid them—you must still not hit a pedestrian
Maintain speed; they are jaywalking and have no rights
Honk and drive through
Speed up to pass before they reach your lane
questions.explanation: Even where a pedestrian crosses unlawfully, you must do everything reasonable to avoid a collision. Their error doesn't give you permission to hit them.

questions.question: You are stopped for a pedestrian in a crosswalk on a multi-lane road. The car in the next lane may not see them, so you should:
choices: Stay stopped and be alert; the other driver might illegally pass your stopped car
Wave the pedestrian to hurry across
Pull forward to block the other lane
Honk at the other driver
questions.explanation: A stopped car can hide a pedestrian from drivers in adjacent lanes ('multiple-threat' crash). Stay stopped, stay alert, and don't wave the pedestrian into the unseen lane.

questions.question: A bicyclist is riding in the traffic lane ahead where there is no bike lane. You should:
choices: Follow at a safe distance and pass only with at least 3 feet of clearance when it's safe
Pass immediately, as close as needed
Honk continuously until they move right
Drive in the oncoming lane to pass on a blind curve
questions.explanation: Bicyclists may use the lane. Slow down, wait for a safe gap, and give at least 3 feet when passing—never squeeze by or pass on a blind curve.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road with Bicyclists

questions.question: At 60 mph, your total stopping distance compared with at 30 mph is roughly:
choices: Much greater—braking distance grows with the square of speed
About double
About the same
Slightly less because of momentum
questions.explanation: Doubling speed roughly quadruples braking distance, and reaction distance doubles too. Total stopping distance grows steeply with speed.

questions.question: In heavy, fast-moving traffic, the safest following distance is:
choices: At least 3 seconds, increased to 4 or more as speed and risk rise
Exactly two car lengths at any speed
As close as possible to prevent cut-ins
Whatever keeps you from losing your place
questions.explanation: Use the time-based 3-second rule and stretch it in heavy or fast traffic. Fixed car-lengths don't scale with speed, and tailgating to block cut-ins is dangerous.

questions.question: You're following a car so closely you can only see its bumper. The main risk is that:
choices: You can't see far enough ahead to react to hazards in time
Your headlights will blind the driver ahead
You'll use more fuel
You'll wear out your brakes faster
questions.explanation: Tailgating shrinks your view of the road ahead and your reaction time. Drop back so you can see the traffic situation developing and stop safely.

questions.question: A diamond-shaped yellow sign showing a truck on a downhill grade warns that:
choices: A steep descent is ahead—trucks and all vehicles should check speed and brakes
Trucks are prohibited ahead
A truck weigh station is ahead
Trucks must exit here
questions.explanation: This warning sign means a steep downgrade is ahead. Slow down, gear down, and be ready for slower trucks and possible runaway-truck ramps.

questions.question: A square (vertical diamond on point is different) orange sign with black symbols at a road project most likely shows:
choices: Construction or detour information you must heed
A permanent speed limit
A scenic point of interest
A hospital location
questions.explanation: Orange signs convey construction and detour information. Follow them and watch for changed traffic patterns and workers.

questions.question: A 'DO NOT ENTER' sign (white horizontal bar in a red circle) facing you means:
choices: You must not drive past it—often the exit of a one-way street or off-ramp
Enter slowly with caution
Enter only to turn around
No trucks may enter
questions.explanation: 'DO NOT ENTER' marks a roadway you may not drive onto, such as a one-way street or a freeway off-ramp, to keep you from going the wrong way.

questions.question: A fire truck approaches an intersection against your green light, siren on. You should:
choices: Yield—pull right and stop, even though your light is green
Proceed because you have the green
Stop in the intersection
Turn left to clear the area
questions.explanation: Emergency vehicles override your right of way. Yield by pulling to the right and stopping; never enter or stop in the intersection.

questions.question: You hear a siren but can't tell where it's coming from. You should:
choices: Slow down, stay alert, and avoid changing lanes until you locate it
Speed up to clear the area
Pull left immediately
Ignore it until you see lights
questions.explanation: If you can't locate an emergency vehicle, reduce speed and avoid sudden moves until you see where it is, then pull right and stop as needed.

questions.question: It is illegal to follow a fire engine responding to an alarm any closer than:
choices: 300 feet
100 feet
150 feet
75 feet
questions.explanation: You may not follow within 300 feet of a fire engine, ambulance, or police vehicle running its siren or lights.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Following Emergency Vehicles

questions.question: You're driving and your phone rings through the car's hands-free system. The law allows you to:
choices: Answer with a single button or voice command and keep your eyes on the road
Pick up the handset to talk
Look at the screen to see who's calling for several seconds
Hold the phone to your ear if the call is short
questions.explanation: Adults may use a phone only in hands-free mode, operated by a single touch or voice. Holding the phone or staring at the screen is prohibited.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Cell Phone Laws

questions.question: Which is true about using a phone at a red light?
choices: Texting is still illegal; you are 'driving' even while stopped in traffic
You may text freely while stopped at a light
You may watch videos at a long light
Phone rules only apply while the car is moving
questions.explanation: The cell-phone and texting laws apply whenever you're operating the vehicle in traffic, including stopped at a signal. Pull over and park to handle a phone.

questions.question: Compared with talking to a passenger, a phone conversation while driving tends to be:
choices: More dangerous—a passenger can see hazards and pause the conversation
Exactly the same risk
Safer, because the phone is hands-free
Only risky for new drivers
questions.explanation: A passenger shares the driving environment and naturally stops talking during tricky moments; a remote caller does not, so phone talk is more distracting.

questions.question: Your green light has just turned, but cross traffic is still clearing the intersection. You should:
choices: Wait until the intersection is clear before entering
Proceed at once—green means go
Edge in to claim the space
Honk and accelerate
questions.explanation: A green light gives the right of way only when the intersection is clear. Yield to traffic and pedestrians still finishing their crossing.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Traffic Signal Lights

questions.question: A lane over the freeway shows a steady yellow X. This means:
choices: The lane is closing ahead—prepare to move out of it safely
The lane is open for use
Stop in the lane
Carpools only may use the lane
questions.explanation: A steady yellow X warns that the lane is about to close; merge out of it when safe. A red X means it's closed; a green arrow means it's open.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Lane Use Signals

questions.question: At an uncontrolled intersection (no signs or signals) you and a car on your right arrive together. You should:
choices: Yield to the car on your right
Proceed first because you're going straight
Proceed because you're on the larger road
Wave the other car through and then race across
questions.explanation: With no controls and a tie, yield to the driver on your right. Slow down and be ready to stop at any uncontrolled intersection.

questions.question: You're turning left from a driveway onto a busy two-way street. You must yield to:
choices: Traffic from both directions and any pedestrians on the sidewalk
Only traffic coming from your left
Only traffic coming from your right
No one, if you signal
questions.explanation: Turning left out of a driveway crosses both directions of traffic plus the sidewalk, so you must yield to all of them before going.

questions.question: Two cars face each other across an intersection; both have green lights. One goes straight, the other wants to turn left. The left-turning driver must:
choices: Yield to the oncoming car going straight
Turn first because they signaled
Proceed together with the oncoming car
Expect the straight car to stop
questions.explanation: On a plain green, a left-turning driver must yield to oncoming traffic going straight or turning right. Only a green arrow gives a protected left.

questions.question: A flashing yellow beacon over a school-zone sign is dark (not flashing) at 8 p.m. This means:
choices: The reduced school-zone limit is not in effect; the normal limit applies, but stay alert
You must still drive the school-zone speed
The road is closed
You must stop before the sign
questions.explanation: When the beacon isn't flashing and children aren't present, the reduced limit usually doesn't apply. Obey the regular limit, but remain watchful.

questions.question: A school bus stops with red lights flashing on a road divided by a raised concrete median, the bus on the opposite side. You:
choices: May proceed with caution without stopping, because a barrier divides the road
Must stop because the lights are red
Must stop only if children cross the median
Must wait until the bus moves
questions.explanation: A raised median or barrier means opposing traffic need not stop for the bus. On an undivided road (even with a painted center line), both directions must stop.

questions.question: You take a prescription painkiller that warns 'do not operate machinery,' then drive and feel drowsy. You:
choices: Can be arrested for DUI if your driving is impaired
Are exempt because it was prescribed to you
Are fine as long as you drive carefully
Are only at risk if combined with alcohol
questions.explanation: DUI law covers impairment from any drug, including a properly prescribed one. Heed 'do not operate machinery' warnings and don't drive while affected.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Drugs and Driving

questions.question: The amount of alcohol in one 12-oz beer, one 5-oz glass of wine, and one 1.5-oz shot of liquor is:
choices: About the same—each is roughly one standard drink
Highest in the beer
Highest in the wine
Highest in the shot
questions.explanation: Each contains a similar amount of pure alcohol—about one standard drink. 'Just a beer' impairs you about the same as a glass of wine or a shot.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Alcohol and the Body

questions.question: At a checkpoint you are lawfully arrested for DUI and asked to take a breath or blood test. If you refuse:
choices: Your license is suspended automatically and penalties increase
There is no penalty for refusing
You simply get a warning
The arrest must be dropped
questions.explanation: Implied consent makes a chemical test mandatory after a lawful DUI arrest. Refusal brings an automatic suspension and added penalties.

questions.question: You signal and begin a lane change, then see a motorcycle you'd missed now alongside you. You should:
choices: Abort the lane change and return fully to your lane
Continue, since you already signaled
Speed up to move ahead of the motorcycle
Edge over slowly to make room
questions.explanation: Motorcycles are easy to miss. If one appears beside you mid-maneuver, cancel the lane change and stay put until it's clearly safe.
questions.handbook_reference: California Driver's Handbook — Sharing the Road with Motorcycles
